subject: Request: per-route token-phase breakdown + prototype dashboard (Brightline spike context)
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Alejandra Torres <a.torres@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: Brightline Health CS <cs@brightlinehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 7 May 2029 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Request: per-route token-phase breakdown + prototype dashboard (Brightline spike context)

Team / Alejandra —

Quick context: Brightline experienced a cost spike on 2029-04-30 that their SRE flagged as a sudden increase in token spend tied to one of their chat endpoints. They passed along the sample payload and our SLO exception request (attached).

As part of our post-mortem and to unblock Brightline’s renewal conversation, I want a compact console view that shows per-route cost and latency split by "token phases":
- prompt (tokens sent to model)
- generation (tokens produced by model)
- tool-calls / function payloads (if applicable)

Ask: can we prototype a per-route tile that surfaces the token-phase cost split (absolute and pct), 95th latency by phase, and an obvious callout when a recent SLO exception exists? The goal is a short demo for Brightline CS + SRE next week and an internal story for prioritization in the Observability roadmap.

What I need from you:
- Dylan: instrument definitions + quick query (one-off) that can run for the Brightline tenant and produce the three-phase breakdown for the last 30 days.
- Jonas: an estimate for query cost and sampling strategy if we need to avoid full re-ingest.
- Irene/Marissa: a rough UI/UX mock (one tile) and the minimum telemetry fields you need to render it.

Attachments: spike-sample-20290430.json, slo-exception-notes.pdf

Timing: Brightline indicated Thursday afternoon (their timezone) works for a 30-min demo; ideally we have a working prototype by Wednesday EOD for internal review.

Thanks —
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Group Product Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Alejandra Torres <a.torres@brightlinehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 7 May 2029 10:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Request: per-route token-phase breakdown + prototype dashboard (Brightline spike context)

Thanks Tessa — quick first pass from infra/metrics perspective.

Definitions I propose (so we have a common language):
- prompt_tokens: tokens in the request payload sent to the model (includes system + user + context).
- generated_tokens: tokens emitted by model, counted until the final stop or truncation.
- tool_tokens: tokens exchanged with external tools (tool input + output) when tool-calling is used; if not instrumented, mark as unknown.

Query outline I can run today against Brightline’s tenant:
- timeframe: 30d, group by route_id
- produce: sum(prompt_tokens), sum(generated_tokens), sum(tool_tokens by type), avg/95latency_prompt, avg/95latency_gen, count(requests)

Caveats:
- We currently only have explicit tool_tokens for v2.1 instrumented routes; older routes will show tool_tokens=null.
- Sampling: if we run full-resolution for 30d on high-traffic tenants it could be expensive; I recommend a 10% deterministic sample for the prototype unless Jonas prefers a short window.

I can drop the one-off CSV by EOD.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior SRE, Inference Platform

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Alejandra Torres <a.torres@brightlinehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 7 May 2029 13:27:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Request: per-route token-phase breakdown + prototype dashboard (Brightline spike context)

High-level UI constraints and asks from Console:

1) Telemetry fields needed (minimum): route_id, tenant_id, timestamp, prompt_tokens, generated_tokens, tool_tokens (optional), latency_prompt_ms, latency_gen_ms, request_id, slo_exception_flag

2) Mock idea: a compact tile that shows a stacked bar (prompt/gen/tool) with hover showing absolute counts and per-token cost (we can derive cost if we have token->unit mapping). Right-hand column: 95th latency by phase and a small badge for SLO exceptions with link to the exception page.

3) UX tradeoffs: for a first prototype we should avoid per-request expansion (too heavy). Aggregate rows (by route) with drill-to-results is fine. We can hardcode Brightline’s cost-per-token mapping for the demo.

Deliverable: Marissa and I can produce a clickable Figma tile and a Storybook component stub if Dylan provides the CSV by EOD tomorrow. If Jonas indicates sampling will drop accuracy >10%, call that out — we’ll surface an accuracy note on the tile.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Product Design, Console Team

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Alejandra Torres <a.torres@brightlinehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 8 May 2029 08:15:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Request: per-route token-phase breakdown + prototype dashboard (Brightline spike context)

I ran a quick capacity / cost read on the proposed query. Results and recommendation below; attaching a small sampling plan.

Short answer: feasible for a prototype with bounded cost.

Estimate:
- Full-resolution 30d, tenant Brightline (peak ~2k reqs/min): ~6k query throughput units, estimated infra cost ~ $420 (one-off) + 2h engineer time to sanity-check data joins.
- 10% deterministic sampling (by request_id hash) reduces cost ~10x and gives stable aggregates for prompt/gen totals with ~±5% noise on high-volume routes.

Recommendation:
- Prototype: run 10% sample across 30d, generate per-route aggregated CSV and a separate 7d full-resolution window for the top 3 routes.
- Production: we need to add tool_tokens to older instrumentation or fallback to heuristics (request/response length diffs) which I flagged as higher error.

Attachments: per-route-sampling-plan.csv

If you want, I can kick off the sample job tomorrow morning and drop the CSV in our shared drive (link below).

Shared drive: https://drive.redwood.company/shared/observability/brightline-prototype

— Jonas
Data Platform Lead

From: Alejandra Torres <a.torres@brightlinehealth.com>

Two quick asks from our side for the demo:
- if possible, include a short note showing how a per-route tile ties to billing (simple mapping) so our finance folks see the line-item.
- please include a one-slide note on limitations (sampling accuracy + tool token coverage).

I’ll loop in our CS lead (cs@brightlinehealth.com) in a follow-up so they can join the demo invite.

Best,
Alejandra
